s1.syndrome_frame: a subacute onset of a localized breast lesion with associated discomfort
salient_findings: palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
spiculated lesion on breast MRI with early enhancement peak
cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells on excisional biopsy
key_facts: 62-year-old woman
one-month history of burning sensation and discomfort in her left breast
no fever or systemic symptoms
history of hypertension
remote history of hemorrhoidectomy, dilation and curettage, colonoscopy, and gastroscopy
heavy smoker
3 × 3 cm palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
no axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
unremarkable routine blood tests, chest radiograph, and ECG
breast MRI showed an ill-defined, deep retroareolar spiculated lesion
excisional biopsy showed breast tissue containing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells
epithelial cells positive for cytokeratin AE1/E3 and negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu

shortlist.label: Triple-negative breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Epithelial cells are negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, which is consistent with triple-negative breast cancer

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells and a palpable mass are consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma

shortlist.label: Medullary carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphoid infiltrate and negative hormone receptor status are consistent with medullary carcinoma

shortlist.label: Metaplastic carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a palpable mass and negative hormone receptor status are consistent with metaplastic carcinoma

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid onset of symptoms and presence of a palpable mass, although no skin changes are noted
